claim: SemiAnalysis's proprietary model estimates Mac gross margin expanded from roughly 28.5-29% to 39.5% after Apple's Intel-to-Apple-Silicon transition, a 10.5-11 percentage point expansion (the article states both figures internally, an unresolved inconsistency).
stance_target: Owning silicon is load-bearing for margin
scope_conditions: Mac product line only; third-party proprietary model, not Apple-disclosed; Apple does not break out margin by product
quoted_support: Mac GM expanded from 28.5% to 39.5% after ditching Intel, an 11-percentage point expansion. ... Mac Gross Margin: 29% (Intel, 2019) to 39.5% (M3 Pro, 2023) = 10.5pp expansion

claim: SemiAnalysis estimates iPhone gross margin grew 5 percentage points, from 36.5% (A4 era) to 41.5% (A18 era), attributable in part to in-house silicon.
stance_target: Owning silicon is load-bearing for margin
scope_conditions: iPhone product line only; modeled estimate, not Apple-disclosed

claim: SemiAnalysis estimates Apple's annual chip cost savings from in-house silicon (vs. merchant silicon) exceed $7 billion, broken out as roughly $5B from Intel displacement, $1.2B from Qualcomm displacement, $700M from Broadcom displacement, and $500M+ from custom IP.
stance_target: Owning silicon is load-bearing for margin
scope_conditions: Modeled estimate; unclear whether this is gross COGS saving or nets out design/R&D cost
quoted_support: Annual chip savings exceed $7B across Intel, Qualcomm, and Broadcom displacement. ... Annual Chip Savings: $7B+ (Intel $5B + Qualcomm $1.2B + Broadcom $700M + custom IP $500M+)

claim: Apple expects to eliminate Qualcomm modems entirely from its lineup by 2027-2028, which SemiAnalysis calls a 'gross margin stacking opportunity.'
stance_target: Forward margin effect of in-house modems
quoted_support: By 2027-2028, Apple expects to eliminate Qualcomm entirely in its lineup, offering it a gross margin stacking opportunity.

claim: Apple's silicon manufacturing is deeply and increasingly concentrated at TSMC: Apple's annual TSMC spend grew from $2B (2014) to $24B (2025), a 12x increase, and Apple has consistently accounted for >50% (sometimes near 100%) of demand at new node launches since 20nm.
quoted_support: Apple's annual spend at TSMC grew from $2B in 2014 to $24B in 2025. That is 12x in 12 years. ... consistently >50% since 20nm and in some cases near 100%.

claim: Switching Apple's leading-edge chip manufacturing away from TSMC to Samsung or Intel would cost an estimated $2-5 billion in redesign and requalification, and Samsung's 3nm yields (30-40%) still trail TSMC's 80%+, making near-term diversification of leading-edge silicon manufacturing impractical.
quoted_support: The switching cost was estimated at $2-5 billion in redesign and requalification alone. ... Samsung's 3nm yields were 30-40% versus TSMC's 80%+.

claim: Nearly all of Apple's leading-edge chip production occurs at a single facility, Fab 18 in Tainan, Taiwan, roughly 100 miles from mainland China; TSMC Arizona accounts for under 5% of leading-edge production and will not materially reduce Taiwan dependence until 2028 or later.
quoted_support: Apple's Taiwan concentration is the elephant in the room. Nearly all of Apple's chip production, including every leading-edge A-series and M-series chip, happens on a single island 100 miles from mainland China. ... Currently <5% of leading-edge production is from Arizona.

claim: Apple's historical dominance as TSMC's anchor customer is eroding as AI/HPC demand (led by Nvidia) grows: TSMC HPC revenue share rose from 36% (2020) to 58% (2025) while smartphone share fell from 46% to 29%, and the model projects Nvidia will consume more N3 wafers than Apple by Q4 2027, with Apple's N2 node share dropping to 48% -- the first time in a decade Apple is not the dominant customer on a new node.
stance_target: Silicon ownership as a permanently durable, uncontested Apple advantage
quoted_support: HPC revenue at TSMC grew from 36% in 2020 to 58% in 2025. Smartphone revenue shrunk to 29% from 46%. Our model shows Nvidia will consume more N3 wafers than Apple by 4Q27. Apple's share of N2 drops to 48%, the first time in a decade Apple is not the dominant customer on a new node.

claim: Apple's own SVP of Hardware Technologies frames Apple Silicon as a product-experience decision, not a cost or chip-business decision, directly echoing the Digits to Dollars 'not about money' thesis.
stance_target: Owning silicon is load-bearing for margin (as opposed to differentiation)
quoted_support: First and foremost, if we do this, can we deliver better products? That's the No. 1 question. It's not about the chip. Apple is not a chip company. - Johny Srouji, Apple SVP of Hardware Technologies

claim: TSMC's own gross margin expanded 13.5 percentage points (45.5% in 2010 to 59%+ in 2025) partly on the back of Apple-funded node development, meaning some of the value created by the Apple-TSMC relationship accrued to TSMC's margin, not Apple's.
stance_target: Owning silicon is load-bearing for margin

claim: Apple originally offered TSMC roughly a 40% gross margin on its business, in line with TSMC's margin at the time; current Apple-business gross margin at TSMC is significantly higher than that initial 40%, implying TSMC (not just Apple) has captured pricing power gains from the relationship over time.
scope_conditions: Citing an Acquired.fm podcast interview with Morris Chang
quoted_support: Apple initially said to have offered 40% gross margin to TSMC, which was in line with TSMC's margin then. Current gross margin from Apple business is significantly higher than the initial 40%.

claim: Merchant-silicon competitors (Qualcomm Snapdragon, Intel, AMD) have closed some of the architectural gap with Apple Silicon by 2024-2025 -- reaching decode-width parity (8-wide), adding system-level cache (Qualcomm 8MB SLC, Intel 8MB memory-side cache), and matching Apple's L1 cache size/latency (Qualcomm Oryon, built partly by ex-Apple engineers) -- narrowing but not closing Apple's efficiency lead.
stance_target: Durability of Apple Silicon's competitive/performance moat
quoted_support: Decode width is no longer Apple's moat. ... Qualcomm added 8MB SLC; Intel added 8MB memory-side cache ... Qualcomm Oryon matches Apple's 320KB L1 at similar latency ... The gap has narrowed, but Apple still holds the efficiency crown.

claim: Apple's chip vertical-integration strategy extends well beyond the CPU/GPU: custom silicon now covers audio (H-series), security (T-series), wireless (W-series), ultra-wideband (U-series), spatial computing (R-series), and modems (C-series), acquired/built via five landmark moves: P.A. Semi (2008, $278M), AuthenTec (2012, $356M), PrimeSense (2013, $360M), Intel's modem business (2019, $1B), and the in-house GPU effort that displaced Imagination Technologies (2017).
stance_target: Owning silicon is load-bearing for margin (breadth of vertical integration)
quoted_support: P.A. Semi (2008, $278M) ... AuthenTec (2012, $356M): Touch ID ... PrimeSense (2013, $360M): Face ID ... Intel Modem Business (2019, $1B): In-house 5G Modem ... The Imagination Breakup (2017): In-House GPU
